headline: The UK government has agreed to carry out all 44 recommendations of a commission on how to regulate AI in healthcare.
score_reason: New official decision; acceptance, not yet rules.
importance_line: Patients and the NHS could get AI devices that are watched while in use, but accepting recommendations is not the same as new rules, and the key guidance is not due until December 2026.
summary: Medical Device Network reports that UK ministers accepted all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, whose main proposal, made in September, is that AI medical devices be monitored throughout their working life instead of assessed once. The medicines regulator MHRA is due to publish draft guidance on managing device changes in December 2026, and ministers are exploring staged approval routes that would let the NHS use some tools under close supervision while real-world evidence is collected.
notes: Original Computer Weekly page blocked (403); credited Medical Device Network.
